Just like the title says. Anything distracts her. I have her clicker trained, but Can't seem to get the commands down. For example, she knows down when I do the motion, but when using the words, she just ignores me. It gets to a point where I get frustrated and she just goes into play mode and doesn't listen. Those stupid books don't help much... 7 days she says... ha!

Edit: Toy poodle, not roy....

It sounds like she thinks that the motion is the prompt for the behavior. Basically, it has yet to register with her that she should be listening to your voice commands instead of your body language. Dogs tend to be very context-dependent, so you have to fade out your body language. Sometimes it takes longer to fade for one dog than another.

To fix this, you first need to be very aware of what you are doing with your body. Since a toy poodle is pretty short, are you leaning down to do the hand signal? If so, you can start to fade the hand signal, but keep leaning down until you've successfully faded the hand signal. Then you can start using the vocal command while no longer leaning down quite so far. To fade the hand signal, you need to watch when the behavior occurs. Does she manage to do the behavior right before you finish the hand signal? If so, end the hand signal before you complete the whole motion.

It's definitely a whole process and dogs learn at various speeds. As the people training the dogs, there's a learning curve for us as well. For general distractions, you're best off starting training in a pretty calm and uninteresting environment. If that still isn't making you very interesting, you can use higher-value rewards (chicken, cheese, anything your dog absolutely loves) or you can do something that my school called a 'happy circle.' When doing a happy circle, you move in a little circle very quickly and make a ton of weird/interesting noises.
Good tips. Thanks. I gotta remember to end the sessions before I get too frustrated.

It sounds like you also need to work on slowly increase her attention span. Teaching "focus" is a really good one for this. Reward for eye contract and slowly start to lengthen the time before the reward until she maintains eye contact with you for a longer period of time. The same can apply for basic obedience commands. Teach "sit" and have her hold the sit for increasing periods of time before break and reward. Keep training sessions brief, and always end on a positive note and with something fun. Also you can try using higher-value rewards, depending on what she's interested in. It may be a stinky treat, hot dogs, cheese, pieces of liver, etc.

How old is she? If she's young, she may still be in the puppy stage of getting distracted by anything and everything, and that requires a different training method and teaching approach than if I would be working with an older dog who just doesn't want to listen. The key is consistency, regardless of training method, and steady practice. Don't let the dog pick up on your frustration and end things if you are starting to get annoyed because the dog can pick up on that too. Training sessions should be brief, fun, and always end on a positive note or with the dog doing something correctly.
She is still a puppy. I'll work on extending her focus. Thanks. Right now, she can't hold anything for more than 1-5 seconds.

So with her being a puppy, then I wouldn't have very high expectations. They go through learning stages. I felt like I wasn't making any progress with my puppy for a month or so, and then suddenly he got a bit older and everything clicked for him. And then he got a bit older and decided that other things were more interesting than me again. So expect to go through stages with her as well. Focus is a good one to teach early on though, since it starts reinforcing the idea that you are going to be more interesting than something else 99% of the time. With a puppy though, the most important thing is to keep things upbeat and happy and teach her that good things happen when she sits on command or downs on command. Don't worry about perfection yet. It will come when you have built a good foundation and she grows into her brain.

"Whether the Cavs win or lose, LeBron James should be the Finals MVP" (ESPN Insider)

Thoughts on this?

Let's look at some of the likely MVP candidates (and I'm assuming the Warriors win here, because let's be frank, with homecourt and the momentum on their side, it looks all but finished now):

Steph Curry is the obvious one, but he hasn't really been as dominant as I think people expected. Yes, his averages are high (28.5/5/6 on 46/43/84 shooting), but the 5-23 (including 2-15) shutdown he suffered in Game 2 really hurts him. That being said, he was the MVP this year, as well as this team's leader and best player, so it makes the most sense that he'd win Finals MVP.

But I've been hearing Andre Iguodala's name thrown around quite a bit this series as well. Primarily due to his defense on LeBron (his numbers aren't stellar). But is he really shutting down LeBron? It seems to me that just about every game so far, LeBron has gotten his. His supporting cast is weak, and they tend to run out of gas by the end of the game, but I don't feel for a second that he's been shut down by any defender so far this series. His worst game so far was Game 4 where he ended up with 20/12/8; a near triple-double.

So then we have LeBron, who's averaging 30/11/8 so far, and is due for a huge game on his homecourt tomorrow. Wouldn't surprise me to see another 40-point game in a desperate attempt to force a Game 7.

Beyond all the numbers, though, I have to take into consideration the definition of "Most Valuable". Obviously, in literal terms, LeBron is the most valuable to his team. In an already depleted roster with barely enough alive bodies to field a full team, it's glaringly obvious that this team would struggle to score 50 points without LeBron. If you take Steph Curry off the Warriors, I honestly don't think they miss a beat. Klay is a proven scorer and can lead this team. They're deep enough to sustain their game and scoring without one of their top players. Despite not having much Finals/Championship experience, they still have proven veterans who know how to play and step up. The Cavs roster right now is very young, very inexperienced, and they're all playing way above their heads right now.

Anyway, thoughts on this? I'd like to hear opinions.
